quote: Those who contemplate the beauty of the earth find reserves of strength that will endure as long as life lasts. There is symbolic as well as actual beauty in the migration of the birds, the ebb and flow of the tides, the folded bud ready for the spring. There is something infinitely healing in the repeated refrains of nature—the assurance that dawn comes after night, and spring after the winter.
source: Rachel Carson, The Sense of Wonder, the closing paragraph (Harper and Row, 1965)

evidence.where: Two independent copies were read, a long quotation of the closing paragraph in a Brain Pickings essay on The Sense of Wonder and the Rachel Carson page at Wikiquote, and they agree on all three sentences in this order, including the definite article in spring after the winter, which most short web copies drop.
evidence.edition: The Sense of Wonder (Harper and Row, 1965), the book made from Help Your Child to Wonder, Woman’s Home Companion, July 1956
evidence.locator: the closing paragraph, following the sentence about those who dwell among the beauties and mysteries of the earth

reason: The wording is confirmed by two sources that quote the whole paragraph rather than a fragment, and the trail matches the passage as it is always printed. The printed page of the 1965 book was not seen, so the setting of the dash before the assurance rests on the American book convention rather than on an inspected page; open the book before landing if the mark matters. Carson is new to the year and this is April’s own promise.
